It is a standard protective coating for cathodes in sulfide-based solid-state cells.

proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich phosphate that should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li. Its P-O bonding is chemically compatible with the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte because both share Li and P, which should limit interfacial reaction penalty. It is a standard protective coating for cathodes in sulfide solid-state cells.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4P2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate with P-O bonding that should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. It shares Li and P with the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte, which should limit interfacial reaction penalty, and it is the closest available analogue to the Li3PO4 hypothesis.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 proposals (mp-aaaaaegs, mp-aaaaauhx) used IDs that are not in the available list. Li3PO4 itself is unavailable, so I chose the closest available Li/P-O phosphate.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-containing oxide with a high-valent Nb5+ center that should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. It is a well-established cathode coating for LiCoO2 in sulfide solid-state cells, where it limits Co/S interfacial reactions. The earlier LiNbO3 ID (mp-aaaaafnn) is not in the available list, so this is the available LiNbO3 polymorph.
proposal.motivation: Earlier proposal of LiNbO3 (mp-aaaaafnn) as a wide-gap niobate coating to reduce the interfacial penalty; that ID is not available, so I used the same formula under an available ID.

proposal.hypothesis: LiNbO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-containing oxide with a high-valent Nb5+ center that should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. It is an established LiCoO2 coating in sulfide solid-state cells, where it limits Co/S interfacial reactions. This is the available LiNbO3 polymorph, since the earlier ID is not in the list.
proposal.motivation: Earlier LiNbO3 proposal (mp-aaaaafnn) was not in the available list. The same formula is available under mp-aaabnawv, so I am testing the niobate coating concept under a valid ID.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-containing oxide. Its Zr4+ center is d0 and cannot be reduced or oxidized near 4 V vs Li/Li+, so it should resist oxidation at the LiCoO2 interface. It is a established coating for sulfide-based cathodes, and its oxygen-rich, Li-bearing chemistry should limit reactions with the Li6PS5Cl electrolyte.

LiTaO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-containing oxide with a d0 Ta5+ center that resists reduction and oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. It is the Ta analogue of the LiNbO3 coating concept, and it is a known protective coating for LiCoO2 that should limit Co/S interfacial reactions with Li6PS5Cl.
proposal.motivation: Earlier niobate proposals (LiNbO3, mp-aaaaafnn and mp-aaabnawv) were chemically motivated as wide-gap, Nb5+ d0 coatings to reduce the interfacial penalty. LiNbO3 itself was not in the available list. LiTaO3 is the closest available analogue in that family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3AlF6 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich fluoride. Al3+ is d0 and fluoride anions are very hard to oxidize, so the coating should resist oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. Its Li-F/Al-F bonding is weakly reactive toward Li6PS5Cl, which should limit interfacial sulfide decomposition at the LiCoO2 contact. This is a halide family not yet tested, unlike the earlier phosphate and niobate oxide proposals.
proposal.motivation: Earlier phosphate and niobate oxide coatings for LiCoO2 against Li6PS5Cl were not available by their proposed IDs, and no evaluation outcomes were returned. Trying a fluoride family tests whether a more oxidation-resistant, Li-rich insulator lowers the interfacial penalty.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-containing oxide with a d0 Al3+ center that resists oxidation near 4 V vs Li/Li+. Its Al-O bonding is oxidatively robust and it is a known protective coating for layered oxide cathodes. It should limit Co/S interfacial reactions with Li6PS5Cl better than unprotected LiCoO2. The earlier coating IDs were unavailable, so this is an available alternative from a different oxide chemistry.
